audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Dinah, Shechem/Hamor negotiation, brothers' deceit, circumcision demand, Simeon/Levi retaliation, plunder, and Jacob's fear. Sensitive wording is restrained while preserving the source's moral stakes.

verses.restored: Dinah, daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

familiar.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah... went out to see the daughters of the land.

modern.text: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.

original.text: וַתֵּצֵ֤א דִינָה֙ בַּת לֵאָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב לִרְא֖וֹת בִּבְנ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the land, saw her, took her, lay with her, and humbled her.

familiar.text: And when Shechem the son of Hamor... saw her, he took her...

notes.title: Humbled her
notes.body: Anah is severe in this context and marks harm against Dinah. The sequence saw, took, lay, humbled is not framed as mutual courtship.

modern.text: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region, saw her, he took her and lay with her by force.

original.text: וַיַּ֨רְא אֹתָ֜הּ שְׁכֶ֧ם בֶּן חֲמ֛וֹר הַֽחִוִּ֖י נְשִׂ֣יא הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּקַּ֥ח אֹתָ֛הּ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אֹתָ֖הּ וַיְעַנֶּֽהָ

verses.restored: His soul clung to Dinah daughter of Jacob. He loved the young woman and spoke to the heart of the young woman.

familiar.text: And his soul clave unto Dinah...

notes.title: Love after harm
notes.body: The text uses love language after the harm already named; it does not undo the first act.

modern.text: And his soul was drawn to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young girl and spoke to her tenderly.

original.text: וַתִּדְבַּ֣ק נַפְשׁ֔וֹ בְּדִינָ֖ה בַּֽת יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיֶּֽאֱהַב֙ אֶת הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל לֵ֥ב הַֽנַּעֲרָֽ

verses.restored: Shechem said to Hamor his father, Take this girl for me as a woman.

familiar.text: And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor...

modern.text: So Shechem told his father Hamor, “Get me this girl as a wife.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁכֶ֔ם אֶל חֲמ֥וֹר אָבִ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר קַֽח לִ֛י אֶת הַיַּלְדָּ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter, but his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob kept silent until they came.

familiar.text: And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter...

notes.title: Defiled
notes.body: Tame names dishonor within the social world of the text; it must not be read as blame on Dinah.

modern.text: Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but since his sons were with his livestock in the field, he remained silent about it until they returned.

original.text: וְיַעֲקֹ֣ב שָׁמַ֗ע כִּ֤י טִמֵּא֙ אֶת דִּינָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וּבָנָ֛יו הָי֥וּ אֶת מִקְנֵ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְהֶחֱרִ֥שׁ יַעֲקֹ֖ב עַד בֹּאָֽם

verses.restored: Hamor father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.

familiar.text: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob...

modern.text: Meanwhile, Shechem’s father Hamor came to speak with Jacob.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֛א חֲמ֥וֹר אֲבִֽי שְׁכֶ֖ם אֶֽל יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְדַבֵּ֖ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard. The men were pained and very angry, because he had done disgrace in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter, for such a thing should not be done.

familiar.text: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it...

notes.title: Disgrace in Israel
notes.body: Nebalah means a shameful outrage. Israel here is family identity before later national identity.

modern.text: When Jacob’s sons heard what had happened, they returned from the field. They were filled with grief and fury, because Shechem had committed an outrage in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter—a thing that should not be done.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֨י יַעֲקֹ֜ב בָּ֤אוּ מִן הַשָּׂדֶה֙ כְּשָׁמְעָ֔ם וַיִּֽתְעַצְּבוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיִּ֥חַר לָהֶ֖ם מְאֹ֑ד כִּֽי נְבָלָ֞ה עָשָׂ֣ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לִשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת בַּֽת יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְכֵ֖ן לֹ֥א יֵעָשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Hamor spoke with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a woman.

familiar.text: And Hamor communed with them, saying...

modern.text: But Hamor said to them, “My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר חֲמ֖וֹר אִתָּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר שְׁכֶ֣ם בְּנִ֗י חָֽשְׁקָ֤ה נַפְשׁוֹ֙ בְּבִתְּכֶ֔ם תְּנ֨וּ נָ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Intermarry with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.

familiar.text: And make ye marriages with us...

modern.text: Intermarry with us; give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.

original.text: וְהִֽתְחַתְּנ֖וּ אֹתָ֑נוּ בְּנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ תִּתְּנוּ לָ֔נוּ וְאֶת בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ תִּקְח֥וּ לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: Dwell with us, and the land shall be before you. Dwell and trade in it, and acquire holdings in it.

familiar.text: And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you...

modern.text: You may settle among us, and the land will be open to you. Live here, move about freely, and acquire your own property.”

original.text: וְאִתָּ֖נוּ תֵּשֵׁ֑בוּ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם שְׁבוּ֙ וּסְחָר֔וּהָ וְהֵֽאָחֲז֖וּ בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I will give.

familiar.text: And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren...

modern.text: Then Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁכֶם֙ אֶל אָבִ֣יה וְאֶל אַחֶ֔יהָ אֶמְצָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֑ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תֹּאמְר֛וּ אֵלַ֖י אֶתֵּֽן

verses.restored: Set bride-price and gift upon me very heavily, and I will give whatever you say to me; only give me the young woman as a woman.

familiar.text: Ask me never so much dowry and gift...

modern.text: Demand a high dowry and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask. Only give me the girl as my wife!” The Revenge of Dinah’s Brothers

original.text: הַרְבּ֨וּ עָלַ֤י מְאֹד֙ מֹ֣הַר וּמַתָּ֔ן וְאֶ֨תְּנָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תֹּאמְר֖וּ אֵלָ֑י וּתְנוּ לִ֥י אֶת הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and spoke because he had defiled Dinah their sister.

familiar.text: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully...

modern.text: But because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah, Jacob’s sons answered him and his father Hamor deceitfully.

original.text: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ בְנֵֽי יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת שְׁכֶ֨ם וְאֶת חֲמ֥וֹר אָבִ֛יו בְּמִרְמָ֖ה וַיְדַבֵּ֑רוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר טִמֵּ֔א אֵ֖ת דִּינָ֥ה אֲחֹתָֽם

verses.restored: They said to them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has foreskin, for that would be a disgrace to us.

familiar.text: And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing...

modern.text: “We cannot do such a thing,” they said. “To give our sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace to us.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לֹ֤א נוּכַל֙ לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לָתֵת֙ אֶת אֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ לְאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר ל֣וֹ עָרְלָ֑ה כִּֽי חֶרְפָּ֥ה הִ֖וא לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: Only on this condition will we consent to you: if you become like us, every male among you being circumcised.

familiar.text: But in this will we consent unto you...

modern.text: We will consent to this on one condition, that you become circumcised like us—every one of your males.

original.text: אַךְ בְּזֹ֖את נֵא֣וֹת לָכֶ֑ם אִ֚ם תִּהְי֣וּ כָמֹ֔נוּ לְהִמֹּ֥ל לָכֶ֖ם כָּל זָכָֽר

verses.restored: Then we will give our daughters to you, and your daughters we will take for ourselves, and we will dwell with you and become one people.

familiar.text: Then will we give our daughters unto you...

modern.text: Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will dwell among you and become one people.

original.text: וְנָתַ֤נּוּ אֶת בְּנֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ לָכֶ֔ם וְאֶת בְּנֹתֵיכֶ֖ם נִֽקַּֽח לָ֑נוּ וְיָשַׁ֣בְנוּ אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיִ֖ינוּ לְעַ֥ם אֶחָֽד

verses.restored: But if you will not listen to us to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.

familiar.text: But if ye will not hearken unto us...

modern.text: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, then we will take our sister and go.”

original.text: וְאִם לֹ֧א תִשְׁמְע֛וּ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ לְהִמּ֑וֹל וְלָקַ֥חְנוּ אֶת בִּתֵּ֖נוּ וְהָלָֽכְנוּ

verses.restored: Their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and in the eyes of Shechem, Hamor’s son.

familiar.text: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem...

modern.text: Their offer seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.

original.text: וַיִּֽיטְב֥וּ דִבְרֵיהֶ֖ם בְּעֵינֵ֣י חֲמ֑וֹר וּבְעֵינֵ֖י שְׁכֶ֥ם בֶּן חֲמֽוֹר

verses.restored: The young man did not delay to do the thing, because he delighted in Jacob’s daughter. He was honored above all his father’s house.

familiar.text: And the young man deferred not to do the thing...

modern.text: The young man, who was the most respected of all his father’s household, did not hesitate to fulfill this request, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.

original.text: וְלֹֽא אֵחַ֤ר הַנַּ֨עַר֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַדָּבָ֔ר כִּ֥י חָפֵ֖ץ בְּבַֽת יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְה֣וּא נִכְבָּ֔ד מִכֹּ֖ל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of their city.

familiar.text: And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate...

modern.text: So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and addressed the men of their city:

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א חֲמ֛וֹר וּשְׁכֶ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל שַׁ֣עַר עִירָ֑ם וַֽיְדַבְּר֛וּ אֶל אַנְשֵׁ֥י עִירָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: These men are at peace with us. Let them dwell in the land and trade in it, for the land is broad enough before them. We will take their daughters and give our daughters to them.

familiar.text: These men are peaceable with us...

modern.text: “These men are at peace with us. Let them live and trade in our land; indeed, it is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters in marriage and give our daughters to them.

original.text: הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה שְֽׁלֵמִ֧ים הֵ֣ם אִתָּ֗נוּ וְיֵשְׁב֤וּ בָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וְיִסְחֲר֣וּ אֹתָ֔הּ וְהָאָ֛רֶץ הִנֵּ֥ה רַֽחֲבַת יָדַ֖יִם לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם אֶת בְּנֹתָם֙ נִקַּֽח לָ֣נוּ לְנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ נִתֵּ֥ן לָהֶֽם

verses.restored: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to dwell with us, to become one people: that every male among us be circumcised as they are circumcised.

familiar.text: Only herein will the men consent unto us...

modern.text: But only on this condition will the men agree to dwell with us and be one people: if all our men are circumcised as they are.

original.text: אַךְ בְּ֠זֹאת יֵאֹ֨תוּ לָ֤נוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת אִתָּ֔נוּ לִהְי֖וֹת לְעַ֣ם אֶחָ֑ד בְּהִמּ֥וֹל לָ֨נוּ֙ כָּל זָכָ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר הֵ֥ם נִמֹּלִֽים

verses.restored: Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals be ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell with us.

familiar.text: Shall not their cattle and their substance and every beast...

notes.title: Economic motive
notes.body: The proposal is sold to the city through access to Jacob’s wealth.

modern.text: Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals become ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell among us.”

original.text: מִקְנֵהֶ֤ם וְקִנְיָנָם֙ וְכָל בְּהֶמְתָּ֔ם הֲל֥וֹא לָ֖נוּ הֵ֑ם אַ֚ךְ נֵא֣וֹתָה לָהֶ֔ם וְיֵשְׁב֖וּ אִתָּֽנוּ

verses.restored: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and Shechem his son, and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

familiar.text: And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all...

modern.text: All the men who went out of the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male of the city was circumcised.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ אֶל חֲמוֹר֙ וְאֶל שְׁכֶ֣ם בְּנ֔וֹ כָּל יֹצְאֵ֖י שַׁ֣עַר עִיר֑וֹ וַיִּמֹּ֨לוּ֙ כָּל זָכָ֔ר כָּל יֹצְאֵ֖י שַׁ֥עַר עִירֽוֹ

verses.restored: On the third day, when they were in pain, two sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the city in confidence, and killed every male.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore...

notes.title: Dinah’s brothers
notes.body: The narrative identifies Simeon and Levi by their relationship to Dinah, linking retaliation to family honor and outrage.

modern.text: Three days later, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons (Dinah’s brothers Simeon and Levi) took their swords, went into the unsuspecting city, and slaughtered every male.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י בִּֽהְיוֹתָ֣ם כֹּֽאֲבִ֗ים וַיִּקְח֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי בְנֵי יַ֠עֲקֹב שִׁמְע֨וֹן וְלֵוִ֜י אֲחֵ֤י דִינָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ חַרְבּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ עַל הָעִ֖יר בֶּ֑טַח וַיַּֽהַרְג֖וּ כָּל זָכָֽר

verses.restored: They killed Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and went out.

familiar.text: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son...

modern.text: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

original.text: וְאֶת חֲמוֹר֙ וְאֶת שְׁכֶ֣ם בְּנ֔וֹ הָרְג֖וּ לְפִי חָ֑רֶב וַיִּקְח֧וּ אֶת דִּינָ֛ה מִבֵּ֥ית שְׁכֶ֖ם וַיֵּצֵֽאוּ

verses.restored: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

familiar.text: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and spoiled the city...

modern.text: Jacob’s other sons came upon the slaughter and looted the city, because their sister had been defiled.

original.text: בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֗ב בָּ֚אוּ עַל הַ֣חֲלָלִ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖זּוּ הָעִ֑יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר טִמְּא֖וּ אֲחוֹתָֽם

verses.restored: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, what was in the city and what was in the field.

familiar.text: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses...

modern.text: They took their flocks and herds and donkeys, and everything else in the city or in the field.

original.text: אֶת צֹאנָ֥ם וְאֶת בְּקָרָ֖ם וְאֶת חֲמֹרֵיהֶּ֑ם וְאֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִ֛יר וְאֶת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה לָקָֽחוּ

verses.restored: All their wealth, all their little ones, and their women they took captive and plundered, and all that was in the house.

familiar.text: And all their wealth, and all their little ones...

notes.title: Escalated collective violence
notes.body: The retaliation expands beyond Shechem and Hamor to the whole city and its households.

modern.text: They carried off all their possessions and women and children, and they plundered everything in their houses.

original.text: וְאֶת כָּל חֵילָ֤ם וְאֶת כָּל טַפָּם֙ וְאֶת נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם שָׁב֖וּ וַיָּבֹ֑זּוּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּבָּֽיִת

verses.restored: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, You have troubled me, making me stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanite and the Perizzite. I am few in number, and if they gather against me and strike me, I and my house will be destroyed.

familiar.text: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me...

modern.text: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land. We are few in number; if they unite against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל שִׁמְע֣וֹן וְאֶל לֵוִי֮ עֲכַרְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִי֒ לְהַבְאִישֵׁ֨נִי֙ בְּיֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּבַפְּרִזִּ֑י וַאֲנִי֙ מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר וְנֶאֶסְפ֤וּ עָלַי֙ וְהִכּ֔וּנִי וְנִשְׁמַדְתִּ֖י אֲנִ֥י וּבֵיתִֽי

verses.restored: They said, Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?

familiar.text: And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?

notes.title: Final protest
notes.body: Simeon and Levi end by naming Dinah’s dishonor; the chapter leaves their response morally unresolved.

modern.text: But they replied, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֑וּ הַכְזוֹנָ֕ה יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת אֲחוֹתֵֽנוּ
